newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to reconsider PLO talks -Netanyahu aide.
newsitem.headline: Israel to reconsider PLO talks -Netanyahu aide.

text.p: A top aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday Israel must reconsider talks with the Palestinian Authority after police said they had evidence linking Palestinian officials with the killing of Arab land dealers.
"These things don't square with the will for peace. They don't square with talk of democracy," said Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan.
"They don't square with negotiations and we must consider carefully if we should continue talks with people who represent such fascist theories," he told Israel's army radio.

Netanyahu was slated to convene top cabinet ministers and security officials later on Monday to discuss Israel's response to the latest developments in the month-long affair over Arab brokers who sold land to Jews.

A Palestinian ban on land sales to Jews followed a halt to PLO-Israeli peace talks over the start of construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. Palestinians say such building on land occupied by Israel in 1967 pre-empts promised final peace talks, which have yet to begin under Netanyahu.

Three Arab land dealers have been slain in the West Bank since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen said last month Arabs who sold land to Jews could face the death penalty if convicted in court.
Israeli police arrested six Palestinians on Saturday suspected of abducting a land dealer and later said four of the six worked for a branch of Palestinian security.

"There is solid evidence that one of the Palestinian intelligence branches is responsible for the two (of the three) cases in addition to the kidnapping," police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin told Reuters.
Israel's Haaretz newspaper said on Monday Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule Authority had prepared a list of 16 Arab land dealers and ordered them murdered.

"The list was prepared by the Palestinian Authority and handed to the various (Palestinian) security agencies," the newspaper said, quoting a security source involved in the investigation of the killings.
Netanyahu, in comments broadcast on Sunday night by Israel Radio, did not specify a course of action but said the situation was unacceptable.
"The fact that there were or are murderous attacks against them via or with the encouragement of senior elements in the Palestinian Authority is something we cannot accept," he said.
"We know that he who does not respect his people also does not respect his neighbour," Netanyahu said.
Israeli officials had consistently said they suspected the Palestinian administration was involved in the killings but PLO officials deny it.
"This is nonsense, the Authority is not involved in the killing of those dealers, brokers, traitors," Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen told reporters in self-ruled Gaza.
The man kidnapped on Saturday was known to have co-operated with 34-year-old Ali Mohammad Jumhour, the latest land dealer to be killed in the West Bank, the Israeli police spokeswoman said.
She said a Palestinian intelligence branch, which she did not name, bore responsibility for the killing of Jumhour and Farid Bashiti, the first dealer killed.
Washington and an international human rights group have urged Arafat to forbid retribution against land dealers.
